references.text: Refers to the "mixed multitude" (עֵרֶב) who complained in the wilderness and caused the Israelites to crave meat, the same group that left Egypt together with the Israelites.
Nehemiah separated the "mixed multitude" from Israel after reading the law, showing the consequences of bringing foreigners out of Egypt.
Describes the large number of small and large livestock that were sacrificed, reminiscent of the herds the Israelites took with them from Egypt.
Moses insisted that all the livestock must leave Egypt with them; not a hoof was to be left behind.
The people mention their livestock in the wilderness, the same livestock they brought out of Egypt.
Abram was also rich in livestock (מִקְנֶה) when he set out, a pattern that is repeated at the Exodus from Egypt.
